h: Big Days Out in Cardiff, With a Bowl to Finish
p: Cardiff packs a lot into a compact centre. Cardiff Castle stands right in the middle of town, with Roman walls, a Norman keep and lavish Victorian interiors. The Principality Stadium looms over the River Taff and is famous for its huge match-day atmosphere, whether it's rugby, football or a stadium gig. When there's a big event on, the whole city fills up, so book well ahead if your visit lines up with one.

Cardiff's Victorian and Edwardian shopping arcades are a joy to wander, with independent shops and cafés tucked inside. Down at Cardiff Bay, the Wales Millennium Centre, with its striking slate and steel front, and the Senedd, home of the Welsh Parliament, sit by the water. A short trip out of the centre brings you to St Fagans National Museum of History, an open-air museum of historic buildings from across Wales. Castell Coch, the fairytale castle in the woods north of the city, is another favourite.

Back at the lanes, some tips to keep things smooth. Book early for weekends, and arrive a few minutes before your slot to sort shoes and drinks. Big group? Split into balanced teams and agree a forfeit for the losers. Don't fancy bowling? Every group has someone who'd rather hold the drinks and heckle, and the other games mean they won't feel left out. And if your team loses, there's always the excuse that the Welsh weather put you off your game.
